text:
Your deck buries its best news on slide nine. The 40% month-over-month revenue growth only appears after three slides of generic market-sizing.

Investors skimming a seed pitch decide within the first 3 minutes. According to DocSend's averages, they often spend under 4 minutes on the whole deck. Your traction number is the one your fundraising argument depends on, and it shows up after their attention has gone.

Your opening slide is a mission statement. Put the data up front instead. Slide two should lead with growth, then give the customer acquisition cost payback period of 5 months, then state the problem.

Right now the deck reads like a mystery novel that saves the answer for the end. Readers skip to the last chapter or quit, and investors will assume you hid the number on purpose. Cut the TAM preamble to one line and let the traction speak.
